items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: Frank Walker was the recording director at Columbia Records and he recorded Bessie Smith.

ctx.x: Yeah. Let me see what happened. I got out of college and I played in a college band called the Red Onions and we used to play Jimmy Ryan’s on Monday nights alternating with Wilbur DeParis, where Omer Simeon played. I got to know Omer and he played an Albert system to hell. Hardly had any keys on it. It was like, I don’t know how he played. And so I got him a Buffet. Somebody gave me one and I gave it to him, or he gave me 20 bucks for it or something. I really wanted the horn myself but I couldn’t stand him, he…

RCA, that it was a trust, a worldwide trust, you’re not allowed to have — one company controlling the whole world, you know, the competition. You’ve got to break it up. So Sarnoff decided, for legal reasons, they were going to create an RCA label and never mind the Victor and the dog and phonograph, to show that they really are competing against the English Victor talking machine, whatever. And so the RCA label was started. And Dick and I were in charge of that and we put together — it was great fun to put…
